claim: Gradient compression only produces wall-clock speedups when the network is the bottleneck; with a fast network and optimized communication backend, most compressors' speedups vanish.
stance_target: the claim that on a PCIe Gen2 x4 fabric (the bottleneck case), gradient compression should pay off where it would not on NVLink
scope_conditions: Data-parallel SGD with NCCL; comparison of sign-SGD, quantization, and low-rank compressors
quoted_support: While these works demonstrate speedups over full-precision SGD in some settings, we find that their speedups vanish with a fast network and highly optimized communication backend, even on commodity hardware.

claim: Linear compressors such as PowerSGD can aggregate compressed gradients with all-reduce, whereas sign-SGD and coordinate quantization need a gather, which is why they fail to scale on all-reduce-based frameworks.
stance_target: the claim that only all-reduce-compatible compression composes with DDP on this box
scope_conditions: Data-parallel frameworks relying predominantly on all-reduce
quoted_support: In particular, we note that currently proposed gradient compressors are not linear. Their compressed messages cannot be added up hierarchically, unlike raw gradients. This prevents current compressed SGD algorithms from aggregating gradients using an efficient reduce operation and instead require a gather operation.

claim: PowerSGD compresses gradients more than 120x and cuts communication time by 54% on ResNet18/CIFAR10 and 90% on an LSTM/WikiText-2.
stance_target: the achievable magnitude of communication reduction from low-rank compression
scope_conditions: 16 GPUs, NCCL, 10 Gbit/s network; ResNet18 on CIFAR10 and LSTM on WikiText-2
quoted_support: By compressing gradients more than 120x, we reduce communication time (including coding and decoding) by 54% for RESNET18 on CIFAR10 and by 90% for an LSTM on WIKITEXT-2.

claim: End-to-end wall-clock training time falls 24% for ResNet18 and 55% for the LSTM, with a 1.5x time-to-accuracy speedup at approximation rank 16.
stance_target: the end-to-end payoff of compression when communication dominates
quoted_support: End-to-end wall-clock training time to full test quality is reduced by 24% for RESNET18 and by 55% for the LSTM. ... A speedup of 1.5x in time-to-accuracy (loss=5) is achieved with a rank of 16.

claim: Error feedback is required for biased compressors to converge, and PowerSGD combines it with low-rank updates so aggressive compression does not sacrifice test quality.
stance_target: the correctness constraint on any compression scheme used for real training runs
quoted_support: ii) Error feedback ensures convergence with general biased compressors. iii) Low-rank updates enable aggressive compression without sacrificing quality.

claim: PowerSGD uses generalized power iteration with warm-started approximations from the previous step, avoiding an expensive SVD per iteration.
stance_target: the compute overhead of the compressor itself, which matters when the fabric is slow but the GPUs are also weak
scope_conditions: Low-rank gradient approximation via subspace iteration
quoted_support: a low-rank approximation of the gradient using a generalized power iteration ... To improve the quality of the efficient approximation, we warm-start the power iteration by reusing the approximation from the previous optimization step.

claim: The PowerSGD testbed used 16 GPUs connected through a fast 10 Gbit/s network, so its absolute speedups are a lower bound for what a PCIe Gen2 x4 box would see.
stance_target: the claim that compression gains should be larger, not smaller, on a slower fabric
